verdict.claim: A stored notification with an attacker-controlled icon URL caused the victim ntfy app to fetch the backend /publish URL and create a persistent marker message on agent-topic.
verdict.expected_effect: The backend should now contain a trigger notification whose icon points to /agent-topic/publish with a unique marker, and a separate persisted agent-topic message with that same marker created after the victim app fetched the icon URL; this crosses the threat model boundary because a remote attacker with no code on the device caused the victim app/device to issue a state-changing backend request affecting the victim-subscribed topic.

oracles.check: Read backend topic history with mcbv http-get 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/agent-topic/json?poll=1&since=all' and look for both the trigger icon URL and a separate marker message.
oracles.result: Passed: the history contains message id KUijPfJUiNVK with icon http://10.0.2.2:8080/agent-topic/publish?message=OC_ICON_CSRF_1794197873-1168_FROM_agent-topic and a separate message id 5qGe6Q2iVow2 whose message is OC_ICON_CSRF_1794197873-1168_FROM_agent-topic.

oracles.check: Inspect device logcat for the victim app receiving the trigger, DownloadIconWorker fetching the /publish URL, and then receiving the marker message.
oracles.result: Passed: logcat shows NtfyIconDownload downloading the /publish URL, receiving HTTP 200, then NtfySubscriberService receiving the marker notification.

oracles.check: Confirm from source that notification icons are parsed from untrusted message data and automatically downloaded.
oracles.result: Passed: NotificationParser creates Icon(url = message.icon), NotificationDispatcher shouldDownloadIcon returns notification.icon != null, and DownloadIconWorker builds an OkHttp request to icon.url.

oracles.check: Search current UI for the marker text with mcbv ui-find 'OC_ICON_CSRF'.
oracles.result: Failed/not required: the marker was not visible in the current UI dump, but backend history and logcat confirm the effect.

evidence: D/NtfyIconDownload: Headers received: Response{protocol=http/1.1, code=200, message=OK, url=http://10.0.2.2:8080/agent-topic/publish?message=OC_ICON_CSRF_1794197873-1168_FROM_agent-topic}
verdict.rationale: The observable backend state contains both the stored trigger notification and a distinct persisted marker message with the same nonce, and logcat shows the marker was produced immediately after the victim app's icon download worker fetched the /publish URL. The source confirms icons from incoming messages are trusted enough to enqueue an automatic OkHttp download. This is not merely an attacker-owned local artifact: the effect is a state-changing request made by the victim app/device that persisted data on the victim-subscribed backend topic.
